**Designs saved in 0.29.0 use format 46 and don't open in 0.28.x or older.**

SolidCraft is open-source parametric 3D CAD in Rust: sketch, constrain, extrude, and change a parameter to watch the timeline rebuild. [Website](https://solidcraft.io) · [documentation](https://docs.solidcraft.io/) · [try it in the browser](https://solidcraft.io/app) · [Discord](https://solidcraft.io/discord) · [issues](https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/issues) · [roadmap](https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/blob/main/ROADMAP.md).

## New
- **Interface follows your system language on first start.** With no language saved yet, SolidCraft starts in the system's language: the OS locale on the desktop and the browser's languages in the web app, matched by exact tag first (such as `pt-BR`), then by base language (`de-AT` takes German), then English. A new System choice at the top of Preferences' language list is the default and keeps following the system. A language you picked earlier stays as it is (#10183).
- **Sketch Offset keeps its corners joined.** Offsetting a chain whose corners only meet in position, such as separate lines and arcs held by Coincident constraints or ends within 0.0001 mm, offsets it as one chain: each new corner is where the two offset curves meet, trimmed where they overlap and extended where they fall short, in the preview too. An offset circle from a dimensioned circle no longer reports a degree of freedom (#10089, #8858, #9573).
- **Joints under each component, and show or hide many Browser rows in one drag.** Each component placement in the Browser has a Joints folder listing the joints that attach it, with the placement each one joins it to; the rows click, show and hide, open and right-click like the joint's own. Pressing on a row's eye and dragging over other rows' eyes gives them all the first row's new state, as one undo step. F2 renames a clicked Browser group (#9404, #9681, #10013).
- **Measure starts with your selection.** Opening Measure with one or two vertices, edges or faces selected fills its inputs and shows the result right away. Its distance label and X, Y and Z labels can be dragged off the part, keeping a thin leader to what they measure; a double-click puts a label back (#10234, #9395).
- **Freehand lasso selection:** a new option, off by default. With Lasso on in the Select panel, a drag from empty space draws a freehand loop and selects what is wholly inside it, in a sketch and on the model, following the selection filter and Shift/Ctrl adding (#10185).
- **Point-to-point Align on chosen axes:** Align can move a body along only the world axes you choose, such as Z alone, leaving the other coordinates as they are (#10015).
- **Edit Joint shows both sides and can pick them again,** keeping the joint's type, limits, drive and expressions, in one undo step (#9692).
- **Sketch Chamfer takes several corners at once,** as Fillet does, with the same sizes and one undo step (#8998).
- **Sketch Fillet and Chamfer on two lines that don't meet:** a line that stops short is extended and a line that runs past is cut back to where they meet, then the corner is rounded or cut. A radius of half a side now rounds both its corners, the usual way to draw a slot, and a corner held by Coincident takes a fillet when a dimension measures to it (#8426, #8238, #7778).
- **Paste sketch geometry into another design:** sketch curves copied or cut in one design paste into a sketch in another open design, with the constraints and dimensions among them, in one undo step (#9675).
- **Line tool to tangent arc and back:** a new option, off by default (Preferences › Sketch › Rest on a line's last point to switch to a tangent arc). Hold the pointer still on the chain's last point and the next click ends a tangent arc; the same gesture goes back to lines (#9553).
- **Equation curves in lengths:** an equation curve's variable can carry its range's unit, so a formula over a length range reads as the math does ("Variable has the range's unit" in the dialog) (#9549).
- **Expressions in rectangles and center circles:** rectangle corners and a center circle's radius or diameter can be expressions that follow their parameters (#10251).
- **Gruvbox Light and Gruvbox Dark** replace the six Gruvbox cards, each with a Contrast choice of Soft, Standard or Hard; a saved Gruvbox choice carries over to its family and contrast (#10292).
- **Theme options:** a theme can offer options, listed under the active theme in Preferences, starting with Opacity, and can color its panels and the 3D view background per ribbon tab, with a fade between tabs (Tab colors). Theme file authors get options, overlays and requires in the format (#9805, #9807, #9808).
- **Keep work open across design tabs:** a new option, off by default (Keep dialogs and tools open when switching designs). Each design tab then keeps its open dialog with what was picked and typed, its sketch tool and its toolbar tab (#9656).
- **Turn to isometric for Extrude:** two new options, off by default (Turn the view to isometric when Extrude opens, and Go back to the earlier view when Extrude closes) (#9948).
- **Fit the model after a navigator view change:** a new option, off by default, makes a view cube face, corner or arrow and an axis gizmo tip center the model and fit it from one distance; a new Home and Fit size setting sets how much of the view the model fills (default 100 %) (#10092).
- **Invert the view cube rotation arrows:** a new option, off by default, makes the arrows swing the camera the way they point (#10286).
- **NX mouse mapping:** a new navigation preset with middle-drag orbit, Shift+middle pan, Ctrl+middle zoom and a middle double-click to fit (#10156).
- **Make a part active by sketching on its face:** a new option, off by default (Preferences › Sketch › Sketching on a part's face makes that part active) (#10216).
- **Keep the shape of dark parts:** a new option, off by default, in Preferences › Graphics, shades the view in linear light with a soft sky fill, so dark faces keep a gradient instead of turning black (#9028).
- **Linux: the desktop's own title bar:** set `SOLIDCRAFT_TITLEBAR=system`, or `"titlebar": "system"` in `graphics.json`, to open the window with the desktop's title bar and buttons; without it nothing changes (#9263).
- **Color picker:** every color field's popover has step buttons beside its number fields, H, S and V fields, and a row of the 12 most recent colors (#9398).
- **Assembly mass properties:** `assembly.mass_properties` gives the mass, center of mass and inertia of every occurrence and rigid group (#9717).
- **Ribbon tooltips for every command:** every command on the ribbon now has its help text, from Sketch to Surface, Sheet Metal, Plastic, Inspect and Construct (#9069, #9847, #9868).

## Improved
- **Ribbon click ends the running sketch tool:** a second click on the lit ribbon button of the sketch tool in use ends it, so clicks in the view select again. Turn off Preferences › Sketch › Clicking the running tool's button ends it to have the click start the tool again (#10263).
- **Alignment guides from end points and corners:** while a drawing tool waits for a point, hovering a line or arc end, a rectangle corner or a free point shows the same dotted guide as a center or midpoint. Turn off Alignment guides from end points and corners while drawing to keep only centers and midpoints (#9673).
- **Live viewport details:** the details card of an active analysis or of Section edits its settings in one standard card, with its key, readout and actions. Turn off Live viewport details to keep the read-only analysis keys and the Section dialog (#8614).
- **Preferences** has twelve pages under four headings, with General above them, a profile switcher pinned to the page list and an In profile tag on the profile pages; the settings themselves are unchanged (#9907).
- **Settings are saved as soon as they change,** not only every 30 seconds and at a normal close, so a crash or a forced close no longer brings back old settings; changes not yet applied in Preferences don't reach the settings file, and Show tool at cursor survives a restart (#9711, #9831, #10049).
- **Sketch snapping and drawing:** a rectangle corner snaps to the crossing of two infinite construction lines beyond their end points, 3-Point Circle keeps its snapped clicks as constraints, a center rectangle's center lines up with the axes when dragged, Project gives its new curves the selected line type, and the polygon's Radius and Sides boxes stay clear of the preview (#10285, #9922, #10087, #10009, #10199).
- **Sketch dimensions:** a driven dimension that nothing fixes any more takes a value again on a double-click, and dimension edits work with tangent caps on offsets (#10023, #9494).
- **Edit dialogs** show a stored number with its unit, such as "2 mm" for a fillet radius, in Fillet, Chamfer, Shell, Draft, Offset Face, Revolve, Pipe, Thread and more (#8697).
- **Edit Sketch on the ribbon** edits the selected sketch, or offers the design's sketches, instead of a parameter error (#9829).
- **Delete with nothing selected** asks you to select something instead of showing a parameter error (#9114).
- **Delete in a rolled-back history** builds the later history once when nothing breaks, and the delete reuses what its check computed (#9972, #10090).
- **Exploded View** is grayed out, with the reason, until the design has two components (#9659).
- **Pattern and Mirror dialogs** explain Object Type and say why a clicked sketch isn't taken (#10097).
- **Insert SVG** says why a drawing has nothing to import, such as a file that holds only an embedded picture (#9652).
- **Update Links:** linked designs that changed while the tab was away come back as one undo step, and a linked design changed while the assembly was closed is read again when it opens (#9753, #9872).
- **Properties** on a large assembly measures much faster, shows its progress and stops when closed (#8730).
- **Large designs:** each command costs less outside the geometry, the History builds its rows once per change and draws only the visible ones, the unsaved-changes check runs once per change, a save's backup is a hard link instead of a copy, and Browser hover stays fast with many hidden joints (#9615, #9616, #9617, #9823).
- **Navigation:** wheel and trackpad gestures go on under a value box on the model, touchpad orbit and pan work while a tool's field has focus, Continuous orbit turns about the Orbit around point, and the 3D mouse turns a rolled or upside-down view the way the cap is pushed (#10073, #10253, #9690, #10262).
- **View:** the grid fades between levels while zooming instead of popping, the ground grid stays put in grazing views, and the origin point hides behind bodies as the axes and planes do (#9608, #10031, #10103).
- **Sketch panel** follows Dialog buttons at the top (#9884).
- **Buttons** respond to hover and press in the theme's colors (#5331).
- **Selecting a feature** lights its faces even after a later edit renamed them (#9848).
- **Report a bug:** its window can be dragged by its title (#9934).
- **Save As** renames the design after the new file, including a sample (#10036).
- **Graphics card:** the chosen card is used, or Preferences says when it couldn't be (#9252).
- **BOM:** with Sub-parts in their part's row on, an inseparable part lists its purchased parts under its row (#9794).
- **Parameter CSV import** keeps multiline comments and accepts a file with a byte order mark (#9772).
- **Shortcuts** typed as text are normalized and checked, so `ctrl+shift+t` is `Ctrl+Shift+T`, and a shortcut recorded from a Preferences search result takes the key (#9800, #10058).
- **Render:** the GPU path tracer is set up only when the GPU image method is chosen, so Raster preview no longer uses gigabytes on some Vulkan drivers (#9668).
- **Assistant:** each API agent can have its own reasoning effort, an added agent can be edited, a new tab keeps the agent's sign-in, an installed agent that can't start says so and how to reinstall it, and switching models no longer shows "Method not found" for agents that keep their own model (#10259, #9653, #9669, #9655, #10022).
- **Agent chat:** an agent continues after it creates or opens a design, and its system note reaches agents beyond the Claude adapter, such as Codex and Antigravity (#9980, #9818).
- **MCP server:** `batch` and `execute` take an `expect` of volume, bodies and bounding box and flag a mismatch, a new `check_parameters` tool tries parameter values and puts the design back, `measure` has a short summary form, `body_topology` can list only cylinders, and the server's instructions say how to plan, build and verify (#9904, #9910, #9853, #9903).
- **Scripting:** `select.set` takes a face or edge from a point or an index alone, `document.inspect` in the app reports undo, redo and the path, timeline commands prefer an exact feature name, default assembly names skip names in use, and an exported script reports omitted print faces (#10191, #9632, #9748, #9898, #10235).

## Fixed
- **Sketch:** a drag no longer shrinks a line to a point or throws points far from the sketch, a value that would collapse a line or circle is refused, Extend treats only an end on a circle as held, Break refuses an offset's curves as Trim and Extend do, held solves that can't succeed give up sooner, conflict messages no longer name a missing id, and copying drawn 3D sketch curves works (#9728, #8600, #9837, #9773, #8645, #10208, #9859, #10146).
- **Face attachments:** a sketch or offset plane on a face that a joined body split, such as a lid's underside resting on a case's rim, can attach to it again (#9670).
- **Extrude** with every body hidden stays New Body instead of turning to Cut (#9920).
- **Bodies:** Delete removes the body you selected after a rename, a renamed body stays visible when it takes a deleted body's hidden name, a pasted placement's body renames by its Browser name, and renaming a cut-off frame piece keeps the name on that piece after a rebuild (#9789, #10175, #10026, #10132).
- **Browser:** a sketch hidden and shown before an Extrude still hides once the Extrude uses it, and a click just past a feature's name selects it instead of opening its sketch (#9971, #10213).
- **Construction planes, axes and points** hide with their component's placement (#9791).
- **Feature editor** closes when its feature is removed, for example by Undo (#10027).
- **Move editor** shows the angles a move was made with (#9803).
- **Edit Text** disables Bold when the font has no bold face (#9958).
- **Circular Pattern** no longer shows two fields active at once (#10078).
- **Parameters:** hovering a parameter's name shows one tooltip, with the rename hint, instead of two (#10309).
- **Zebra:** flat faces keep one stripe color while the view turns (#9761).
- **View corner Cancel** cancels an unfinished tool before the sketch (#9584).
- **Sketch pane** stays still at 125 % display scaling (#9598).
- **Assistant:** the agent list and the boxes under the switcher keep the panel's margin (#10179).
- **Sleep:** a window that wakes black recovers its ribbon and panels (#8952).
- **`joint.drive`** stores nothing for a suppressed joint and says what was asked; **`inspect.interference`** refuses an unknown body name, and appearance commands take a placed copy's name; an MCP batch step with an unknown key is refused (#9862, #9856, #7865).

## Translations
German, French and Spanish catch up with the catalog, and Czech, Hungarian, Italian, Dutch, Romanian, Swedish, Turkish, Traditional Chinese, Malay, Indonesian, Galician, Norwegian Bokmål, Bosnian, Croatian, Serbian, Russian, Danish and Ukrainian gain the new strings, the toolbar's command help included. Arabic wording is clearer in several places.

## Compatibility
0.29.0 writes design file format 46 (0.28.x wrote 45). Format 46 adds Align on chosen axes, equation curve variables with their range's unit, and linked design file digests. 0.29.0 opens every earlier design, but 0.28.x and earlier can't open a design saved by 0.29.0. Drawing files (`.scdwg`) are format 1. macOS builds are now made on macOS 15 and still run on macOS 11 and later (#9804).

FieldCraft is open-source CAE pre-processing in Rust: it turns geometry into analysis-ready

## What's new in 0.7.0: agentic hex meshing (#AHM)

0.7.0 is the meshing release: an agent (or you) looks at the part, plans the blocks from how it was built, and gets an all-hex mesh, then checks and repairs it.

- **Block plans from the feature graph.** `geometry.features` replays a SolidCraft design's timeline; `mesh.plan` turns it into blocks (O-grid/butterfly rings round holes and bosses, swept and projected cells) and `mesh.plan.apply` meshes them. Symmetric bodies are meshed by their symmetry and mirrored, conforming on the plane.
- **Sizing.** Local size controls on faces, bodies, boxes and spheres with a growth rate (`mesh.size.*`), honoured by every mesher; curvature-based divisions so curved faces lose at most 0.5 % of volume.
- **Clean-up before meshing.** `geometry.check` finds short edges, slivers and near faces; `geometry.defeature` suppresses holes, fillets and bosses (with a proposal panel); virtual topology merges, absorbs, splits and stitches faces.
- **Quality and repair.** `mesh.quality.mark` tags the bad elements in red; strong relaxation morphs the region round them (now a background job, adjustable reach and guards) and returns its best round; new **Move Nodes** tool to drag nodes on the surface with a ghost of the original and live quality.
- **More meshers.** Octree all-hex for parts a block plan does not suit; hex-to-tet transitions with pyramids; tet sliver and needle removal; the same mesh on every run and every platform.
- **Responsive app.** Plan apply, partitioning and cell meshing run as background jobs with progress and cancel.
- **Fluid.** A GPU backend for the lattice Boltzmann solver (wgpu, checked against the CPU), velocity, pressure and temperature slices, surface colouring and streamlines, heat carried by the flow with buoyancy and the heat into every wall.
- **Verification.** Scordelis–Lo roof and pinched cylinder shell benchmarks join the reference cases.

**Thank you** to @bluecmd for the GPU lattice Boltzmann backend, the flow results view, heat in the flow and a careful Windows test pass, and to @erkinalp for the shell benchmarks.

release.notes:
The camera virtual background grows up in this release: cleaner edges, real device tiering, custom images, a much bigger backdrop gallery, and a fix for a serious bug that affected every recording made with v1 backgrounds.

## The big fix

In v0.1, the virtual background silently never made it into your recordings. The preview looked right, but the segmentation model could not initialize inside the recording worker, so every saved take fell back to the raw camera. v0.2 fixes the worker initialization and adds an end-to-end test that decodes the recorded MP4 and verifies both the person and the backdrop are actually in the pixels. What you preview is now truly what you record.

## Tiered matting engine

Background matting now adapts to your machine instead of running one fixed path:

- Balanced tier: GPU segmentation plus guided edge refinement that snaps the mask boundary onto real image detail (hair, glasses, shoulder line), with temporal smoothing that removes the frame-to-frame edge shimmer.
- Lite tier: a multithreaded CPU path (enabled by cross-origin isolation) for machines without a usable GPU, with reduced resolution and inference cadence while the recording stays at full frame rate.
- A runtime governor watches actual frame budgets and steps quality down before a take ever stutters, then back up when headroom returns. It never upshifts mid-recording.
- A Quality control (Auto, Balanced, Lite) in the Camera tab, with a live tier readout. Auto is the right choice for almost everyone.
- A light-wrap pass settles the person into built-in backdrops so the composite reads as one scene.

An experimental high tier (RobustVideoMatting on WebGPU) is built and ships dormant: onnxruntime-web 1.27 currently mis-executes the model's recurrent path on WebGPU, so the tier is gated off until an upstream fix validates. All plumbing is in place to enable it.

## The Framecast Studio signature backdrop

The backdrop gallery now opens with the Framecast Studio: a moody recording room with a boom microphone, violet-lit gear shelves, and the FRAMECAST wordmark glowing in neon green on a slatted wood wall. It is designed as the signature look for the app. Record on it, publish, and the brand travels with your video. It is also the house backdrop for Framecast's own episodes.

## Bring your own background

You can now import your own images as camera backdrops. Files are downscaled and stored locally in your browser (IndexedDB), appear as removable tiles in the gallery, survive reloads, and never leave your machine. The built-in gallery also grew from 6 to 14 scenes, spanning tastes from a neon loft and a lofi sunset study to a night penthouse, a coastal workspace, a minimal gallery wall, and a fireplace cabin.

## UI and quality of life

- Roll tape now lives in the header rail, always reachable no matter how long a settings tab scrolls.
- The Camera tab is organized into collapsible Framing, Background, and Lighting sections with live summaries.
- The camera defaults to the full frame (1x); head-crop zoom is now opt-in.
- Console typography is far more readable: larger micro-labels, a medium mono weight, calmer letterspacing, and brighter secondary ink in the dark theme, all without losing the console character.

## Under the hood

- Cross-origin isolation (COOP and COEP) is enabled, unlocking multithreaded WASM for the CPU tier.
- A deep multi-agent code review of the new engine surfaced and fixed 8 confirmed defects before release, including failure-cascade dead ends, a wedged-inference edge case, and a service-worker caching policy that could have silently broken future upgrades.
- New regression suites: a real-face person-presence test through a synthetic webcam feed, a WebGL mask orientation guard, tier and governor unit tests, and settings migration tests. 90 unit tests and 17 end-to-end tests.

Everything remains fully local. Nothing ever leaves your machine.

## `@dawcore/transport` engine improvements (#636) + follow-ups

Patch release across 16 packages. Headline work is in `@dawcore/transport@0.0.15`; everything else is the exact-pin dependent cascade plus two small core/wam fixes.

### `@dawcore/transport` 0.0.15 (#637–#644, #646)

- **Worker-driven timer** — the scheduler ticks from a Web Worker `setTimeout` loop (25 ms, `DEFAULT_TIMER_INTERVAL_MS`) instead of `requestAnimationFrame`, so playback no longer goes silent when the tab is hidden. Falls back to a main-thread loop where no Worker can be created (Node/SSR, CSP without `worker-src blob:`), with a watchdog for a Worker that never ticks. `Transport.dispose()` terminates it. New `ended` event when a bounded `play(start, end)` reaches its end; `NativePlayoutAdapter` forwards it to the engine's `onPlaybackEnded` hook. A tick that throws stops the transport (warned once) instead of retrying 40×/s.
- **Frame-lattice clock** — elapsed time is counted in integer context frames snapped to the 128-frame render quantum; seconds are a derived view. Seeks round-trip bit-exactly; pause/resume cycles cannot drift. `ContextFrame` is a distinct brand from `Sample`; `getCurrentFrame()`/`getCurrentSample()` added. Backward context-clock readings are absorbed and reported via a new `discontinuity` event.
- **Fractional tick conversions** — `secondsToTicksExact`/`timeToTickExact` keep fractions through the tempo map and round once at the unit boundary; tempo curves use closed-form integration. Engine and playout gained the same exact conversions.
